title: Ordinary immersion pullback agrees with quotient-tower completed pullback
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, with $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $u:Y\to X$ be a locally closed immersion of schemes, meaning a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. On $T=X,Y$ put $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the canonical coefficient isomorphism $u^{-1}B_X\cong B_Y$ and finite projection identifications [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Ordinary $Lu^*$ is pullback of modules over these ring sheaves; completed $Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ and its comparison $Lu^*K\to Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ are the strict quotient-tower construction of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].

For every derived-complete $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ [def-weil-derived-complete, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] this specified comparison is an isomorphism. Ordinary $Lu^*=u^*$ is exact, preserves derived completeness, and has canonical finite-reduction comparisons $u^*(K\otimes^L_{B_X}(A_n)_X)\cong(u^*K)\otimes^L_{B_Y}(A_n)_Y$ in $D((A_n)_Y)$. These identifications respect quotient transitions, the completion unit and all finite projection maps, including successive quotients. The derived-limit comparison here is the map of strict-tower Roos models induced by the exact, countable-product-preserving inverse image, rather than a choice of a map between unrelated cones. If $K$ belongs to the integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], so does $u^*K$, with the same uniform cohomological interval for its reductions.

proof.text: The DVR and finite-quotient perfectness lemmas check $(R,(\varpi))$: $R$ is Noetherian, $A_1$ is additive torsion, and every $A_n$ is finite perfect. Use [def-pur-completed-coefficient-presentation-transport] for the lifted presentation. The profinite-coefficient comparison identifies $c_u$ by every finite projection. Immersion limit preservation makes $F=u^*$ exact and product-preserving; exact descent is triangulated. By [lem-pur-roos-intrinsic-completeness-equivalence], (i)$\Rightarrow$(iv),(v), complete $K$ is intrinsically complete and its specified quotient unit $\operatorname{comp}_K$ is invertible. The auxiliary distinct prime in that lemma can be $2$ or $3$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-pullback-derived-tower] to $Q_{T,n}=(A_n)_T$: its $\tau$ identifies the finite-ring-linear derived reductions, quotient augmentations and all transitions. Countable products are exact on both sites. Thus [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] gives its specified Roos isomorphism $\lambda_M$. On a K-injective tower resolution its augmentation clause applied to $\gamma=\varepsilon_{X,M}:\Delta_XL_XM\to M$ gives $\lambda_M=\beta_M$: the source adjunct is the identity, and the target adjunct is the defined mate. Its Roos projection equation gives evaluation compatibility. Use the counit-normalization node to identify actual $Lu^*$ and strict completed pullback with these exact constructions, preserving their units and evaluations.

proof.text: The factorization node gives $\alpha^F_K=\beta_{K_\bullet}F_D(\operatorname{comp}_K)$. Both factors are invertible by Steps 1–2, hence so is the actual comparison. Its projections are the quotient augmentations; $\tau$ makes the target the reduction tower of $FK$. Thus $FK$ is derived complete. The strict transition equations include all successive quotients.

proof.text: For integral $K$, its reductions are intrinsically constructible with one interval $[r,s]$. Pass to finite etale origin on $X$, apply finite pullback preserving bounded constructibility and the same $[r,s]$, and return to intrinsic constructibility on $Y$. Step 2 identifies these with the reductions of $FK$; Step 3 supplies completeness. These are precisely the integral definition's conditions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NV-9ae4c0407 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: This re-split repairs the RETURN of 3eb1dc03 as prescribed. The statement is unchanged. Live still carries the Q07 six-step proof, so no other group has superseded this delivery. Nothing is in the dropped list, no SGA is cited, and there is no cycle. The item assembly is 2205 characters in 4 steps. Step 1 checks the adic datum: lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr gives a PID; lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect gives the finite free resolution and finite sets. lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image makes c_u an isomorphism. The last clause of lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation makes u^{-1}(-)⊗B_Y exact and limit-preserving. lem-pur-roos-intrinsic-completeness-equivalence (i)=>(iv),(v) gives intrinsic completeness and invertibility of the specified comp_K; old Step 3, including the Koszul sign, lives inside that lemma. Step 2 cites lem-weil-pbc-reduction-pullback-derived-tower for τ on whole towers, with augmentation, transitions and Q_n-linear evaluations. It cites lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit for λ and its projection equation. Applying its augmentation clause on a K-injective tower with γ=ε gives λ=β (checked). Step 3: α^F=β·F_D(comp) is invertible, the actual α=d^{-1}α^F e is invertible, and τ makes this FK's own reduction limit, which is completeness. Step 4 is old Step 6 unchanged, with [r,s] preserved. New node lem-sf-exact-pullback-counit-normalization (2576 characters) is true: G is exact, so its universal counit ε is invertible; F_D with ξ is also an absolute derived functor, so e is unique because Q_X is a localization. New node lem-sf-completed-pullback-mate-factorization (2528 characters) is true for every K by the adjunct expansion and the triangle identity; its projection equations are correct. Cases u=id, Y empty, K=0 and K=A_1 were checked. Neither node is a duplicate: lem-weil-pbc-pulled-reduction-strict-tower-comparison identifies α with the completion unit of N, a different and circular route; def-sf-pull-completion-comparison and lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison are different. Neither node restates an item clause. Every old argument is placed in a new or existing node, and the two new nodes are of comparable size. Advisory: the def-pur-completed-coefficient-presentation-transport citation in Step 1 is barely needed. No fixes.
